items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: He was the head of the woodwind department there and my goodness I studied with him for a long, long time. A long apprenticeship.

ctx.x: What was your experience at Berklee like?

Well I was a private student of Joe’s. Joe Viola’s. I was just a private student. I never studied there. But I used to sit in the hall and listen to all the students there talk about whatever. And Joe occasionally used to sneak me into an ensemble or something like that, to give me a little experience or a sax quartet or a sax section or something. But by and large my association was with Joe Viola. He was the head of the woodwind department there and my goodness I studied with him for a long, long time. A long…
Did he use the keyboard to teach you improvising? I’ve always been curious as to how people teach improvising, if they don’t provide some kind of harmonic set-up.
